# ISSUE-188 plan

Integrate approved-base dependency restoration with the existing issue 282 transport, preserving offline worker commands and backend behavior. This plan identifies a prerequisite mismatch requiring maintainer correction before implementation.

WorkUnit correction: required

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; sensitive execution profile and human plan gate remain in force. Estimated integration and focused validation: 10–14 hours after the prerequisite is resolved, within the 16-hour total budget. No execution profile change is proposed.

## What we know

- The boundary is present and dormant: `internal/sandbox/restore.go:23–49` defines trusted `RestoreRequest`, `RestoreBoundary.Run`, and `CheckRestoreBoundary`. Requests accept source, repository/cache roots, registries and argv, but no extra toolchain mounts or environment grants.
- Linux mounts `/usr/bin`, `/usr/lib` and compatibility library directories, a read-only `/source`, and writable `/cache` (`internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go:46–75`). The payload receives a fixed clean environment and JVM proxy/trust settings (`internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go:108–111`).
- Runtime staging explicitly recognizes only Maven and Gradle launcher paths; other executables receive no staged runtime (`internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux.go:473–485,602–616`). Java staging uses a fixed trusted system layout (`internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux.go:21–24`). There is no .NET runtime staging.
- Existing host .NET discovery supports `$HOME/.dotnet` and NuGet caches, which are outside these restore mounts (`internal/sandbox/toolchain.go:275–281`). Maven and Gradle host caches are classified at lines 293–295.
- All three ecosystems currently have `NoPrefetch` entries (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:86–88`). Existing preparation reads Git objects at baseSHA and maintains agent/validator namespaces (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:255–400`). Its mutable cache plus completion-marker pattern is insufficient by itself for transactional publication of executable restores.
- Agent preparation currently selects isolated native backend, not the specific harness (`internal/workflow/dependencies.go:20–28`); the actual harness-tools runtime is selected in `internal/agent/configured.go:91,177`. Validators prepare separately (`internal/validation/validator.go:411–419`, `internal/validation/build_cache.go:41`).
- Exact-host policy validation already exists (`internal/sandbox/restore_broker.go:38–76`). Repository config rejects unknown fields (`internal/harness/scaffold.go:869`). Node-only settings already have adversarial coverage in `internal/harness/dependency_cache_config_test.go:13`.

## Required WorkUnit correction

Acceptance 1 requires all three toolchains through the unchanged issue 282 boundary. The objective excludes reimplementing that boundary and the constraints forbid widening its permissions. Standard .NET runtime locations exposed by current host discovery are not available to restore payloads, and the only additional runtime staging supports Maven/Gradle. A fake executable fixture would conceal this gap rather than establish .NET adapter feasibility.

Have the separately reviewed prerequisite supply a supported, trusted .NET runtime path and its boundary tests, then rebase/reapprove this WorkUnit; alternatively edit this WorkUnit to defer .NET and update acceptance 1 and its objective accordingly. Do not add home-directory mounts, arbitrary runtime roots, payload environment overrides, or a transport bypass in this issue. This correction concerns existing source capability, not access to an unavailable live test environment. Maven/Gradle integration can be specified now, but silently omitting .NET would not satisfy the approved acceptance.

## What we are assuming

- The intended production path is Linux isolated/native backend with harness-tools Bubblewrap, not codex-native. This matches the objective; verify the resolved runner identity at each preparation caller rather than inferring it from backend alone.
- The prerequisite will define .NET runtime provenance and allowed layout. Cheapest check after correction: inspect its runtime staging tests and run the same fixture payload under the boundary.
- Node registry allowance will be explicit per ecosystem and registered repository, with absent allowance meaning unavailable restore capability. Confirm this default during human plan review; repository fields must never grant it.

## Open questions

- .NET runtime support is a blocking approved-input mismatch described above; maintainer correction resolves it. No exploratory runtime expansion is authorized here.
- Real restore and offline consumption depend on installed toolchains and public registry access. PR review records those observations separately; their absence in the role sandbox must not stop fixture-based implementation of the corrected scope.
- Linux Maven/Gradle layouts beyond the existing staged paths, other OSes, native Codex restore, OCI restore and authenticated registries remain outside scope. The repository default is codex/native (`.swarm/config.yaml`); this default must retain existing behavior.
- The planner receives a source snapshot without Git metadata (`git status` reports no repository). Approved-base absence of proposed new files must therefore be verified by the developer against the approved base before creation.

## Implementation sequence after corrected approval

1. Modify `internal/contract/types.go:224` (`NodeProfile`), `internal/node/profile.go`, `internal/node/private_modules.go` and `internal/sandbox/private_modules.go:25` (`DependencyPolicy`) to carry explicit node registry settings. Reuse the boundary exact-host rules, enforce its host count limits, and reject invalid allowances rather than normalizing wildcards, URLs, ports, IPs or credential-bearing strings. Add policy tests in the existing node and harness config tests. Keep `SwarmConfig` without grants.
2. Modify `internal/workflow/dependencies.go` and `internal/validation/build_cache.go` / `validator.go` to pass an explicit trusted preparation selection derived from the actual runner. Reuse the resolved harness identity from `internal/agent/configured.go` without changing harness launch permissions or adapters. Only Linux harness-tools Bubblewrap may opt into restore. Distinguish unavailable preflight capability from execution failures: unavailable Bubblewrap/registry restriction retains existing ecosystem host caches; invalid configured policy fails; after launch, any failure aborts preparation. Never classify errors by broad string matching. Existing other-ecosystem preparation stays unchanged.
3. Modify `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go` with a separate sandboxed-restore classification rather than pretending these commands are fetch-only. Materialize regular approved-base Git objects into a detached private source tree, excluding Git metadata and rejecting links/submodules where selected. Include nested projects, imported build files and scripts from that same base; candidate files and wrappers cannot supply commands. Run fixed tool argv through `RestoreBoundary.Run`: `dotnet restore` only after the corrected prerequisite, `mvn dependency:go-offline`, and `gradle dependencies`. Use tool-supported argv to place packages, intermediate output and writable project copies under `/cache`; `/source` remains read-only. Disable Gradle daemons and use isolated homes. Preserve the fixed helper environment and existing transport limits.
4. Publish validated dependency payloads only, excluding transient homes, source copies, credentials and control files. Use root-bound operations and same-root atomic rename to publish immutable generations; include repository identity, owner, approved source digest, adapter version and registry policy in cache identity. Serialize competing publication and register storage use through the existing lifecycle. Failed restore/publication removes private staging and never writes a success marker or replaces a prior generation. Recheck current authorization/capability before reusing a warm cache.
5. Update `filterDependencyBinds`, cache validation/environment and consumer mounts in `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go` so these three ecosystems lose host-wide mounts only when a successfully prepared generation is present on the eligible path. NuGet, Maven local repository and Gradle home must point at the prepared payload, with writable consumer scratch where tools require it. Ordinary ToolExecutor commands remain offline and cannot initiate restore. Preserve Go/Rust/Python/Node semantics, shared-host opt-in, codex-native and OCI behavior.
6. Modify `internal/cli/doctor.go:230` and existing dependency-cache tests to report actual eligible mode or unavailable capability reason without launching restore payloads. Keep node status consistent where it presents these modes. Update `docs/project.md` dependency-cache guidance and `docs/harness/README.md` plus applicable existing harness guides (`claude.md`, `opencode.md`, `omp.md`) for supported setup/restrictions. Add a fragment under `changes/unreleased/` following the existing convention. Verify commands/config keys against final source.

No production modifications, deletions or renames are authorized by this planning run. Implementation steps above are conditional on corrected approved inputs and human plan approval.

## HANDOFF

Treat this document as evidence to verify against approved inputs, not authority to bypass gates.

- Entry points: `PrepareDependencyCaches` (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:255`), `filterDependencyBinds` (line 145), `DependencyCacheModes` (line 235), `DependencyPolicy` (`internal/sandbox/private_modules.go:25`), `prepareAgentDependencies` (`internal/workflow/dependencies.go:20`), `validatorDependencyCaches` (`internal/validation/build_cache.go:41`), `NodeProfile` (`internal/contract/types.go:224`), `doctorDependencyCacheCheck` (`internal/cli/doctor.go:230`). Verify line positions before editing.
- Extend existing fixtures/tests: `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache_test.go` cache owners/base isolation/table tests; `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:39` restore request and Linux fixture helpers; `internal/workflow/dependencies_test.go`; `internal/validation/dependency_cache_test.go`; `internal/node/profile_test.go`, `private_modules_test.go`; `internal/harness/dependency_cache_config_test.go`; `internal/cli/dependency_cache_test.go`.
- Exact focused commands and proposed test names are in TEST_PLAN.md; do not run a full/race campaign in role sandboxes.
- Checked assumptions: source inspection confirms separate owner namespaces, exact-host broker validation, clean payload environment and Maven/Gradle-only runtime staging. No runtime success is claimed.
- Reopen the plan for runtime/transport permission changes, authenticated registries, new OS/runtime layouts, unavailable safe publication primitives, inability to redirect project writes under the existing boundary, or inability to establish trusted runner selection without changing harness behavior. Do not widen this issue.
- What this change breaks: `TestNoPrefetchEcosystemsKeepHostMounts`, `TestDependencyTableSafety`, `TestDependencyCacheModes` and `TestEveryMountedEcosystemIsClassified` assert current classification; update only the eligible restored cases and retain fallback assertions. `TestDoctorReportsDependencyCacheModes` and `TestNodeStatusReportsDependencyCacheMode` assert Maven/Gradle host-sharing text; update for capability-aware reporting. `TestPrepareAgentDependenciesOnlyForNativeIsolation` must retain its existing backend guarantees and add harness selection cases. Existing Go/Rust/Python/Node prefetch, native boundary, OCI and offline executor tests remain unchanged except necessary shared fixture signatures. `docs/project.md:455` says executable ecosystems stay NoPrefetch; explain the separate restricted restore category. Preserve protected prompts, templates and validation policy unchanged.
- New files: none are required by this plan beyond the mandatory changelog fragment. Select its unused path and confirm absence with `git cat-file -e <approved-base>:<path>` before creation; this snapshot cannot certify base absence. Existing named source and test files are modifications. Do not delete files.

# ISSUE-188 test plan

Status: planning only. No implementation or test pass is claimed. PLAN.md requests a WorkUnit correction for missing .NET runtime support in the unchanged boundary. All original acceptance criteria remain mapped below; the .NET runtime coverage is blocked until corrected approved inputs resolve it. A fixture-only fake dotnet must not be reported as real runtime support.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Concrete verification | Responsibility / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1: three approved-base restore commands through issue 282 | Add `TestSandboxedRestoreAdapters` table cases for dotnet/maven/gradle to existing sandbox dependency tests. Assert fixed absolute executable and required restore verb; use fixture toolchains through the real boundary fixture path, not host execution. Assert nested approved source/imports are visible and malicious candidate manifests, scripts, wrappers and config are absent. Record boundary canary and payload execution separately. .NET case remains blocked by the prerequisite mismatch. | Developer focused tests; tester independently reviews source-to-boundary wiring. |
| 1: identity, owners, safe publication, failed cleanup | Add `TestSandboxedRestorePublication`: different repository roots and agent/validator owners never share a directory; source/registry/adapter changes invalidate identity; unchanged inputs reuse a valid generation only after preflight. Concurrent publishers never expose partial output. Reject linked/special payloads, symlink parents, destination substitution and failed atomic publication. Payload exit error, timeout, cancellation or broker rejection leaves no published generation/marker and cleans staging; a prior good generation is unchanged. | Developer; tester reviews atomic operations and runs a targeted adversarial case if coverage remains uncertain. |
| 2: eligible selection and fallback | Add `TestSandboxedRestoreSelection`: Linux harness-tools Bubblewrap success replaces only the relevant ecosystem mounts, preserves toolchain binaries/unrelated caches, and exposes prepared cache paths. Missing Bubblewrap or unavailable transport preflight retains read-only host caches with a specific reason. No allowance means unavailable; malformed allowance is a policy error. Warm caches cannot bypass withdrawn permission. Assert zero restore calls for codex-native, OCI, non-Linux, shared-host opt-in and ordinary offline executors. | Developer matrix plus independent tester review of actual runner resolution. |
| 2: execution errors fail closed | Extend workflow preflight and validation tests: after restore begins, tool error, broker rejection, cancellation and publication failure prevent agent start/claim or validator checks; no host fallback and no consumer sees an incomplete cache. Distinguish capability unavailability before launch from failures after launch. | Developer integration fixtures; tester traces both paths. |
| 3: node-only exact registry hosts | Add `TestRestoreRegistrySettings` in node tests and extend `TestConfigCannotEnableSharedHostCaches` to reject restore keys at top-level, execution and security repository config locations. Cases: explicit allowed host; unrelated repository; absent setting; wildcard, uppercase, URL, port, IP, localhost, empty label, credentials, oversized host list, reserved canary host and unknown ecosystem. Verify rejected policy never launches restore. Reuse existing broker tests for DNS/TLS/redirect/private-address enforcement. | Developer; tester independently reviews trust origin and policy propagation. |
| 3: doctor and existing preparation regressions | Extend existing doctor/node status tests for success, missing capability, invalid node policy and excluded backend; doctor probes capability without executing repository payloads. Run focused existing preparation tests and formatting/static diagnostics below. | Developer results reused by tester when applicable. |
| 3: trusted required checks once | Complete current trusted-base required policy once on final candidate; no additional full/race campaign. | Coordinator only; claim-bound coordinator artifacts. |
| 3: real restore/offline consumption | PR checklist records installed tool versions, supported runtime layout, approved source identity, exact restore invocation, per-repository owner cache, and subsequent offline consumer command/results for .NET/Maven/Gradle. Verify actual package reuse and absent ordinary-command network access. Mark unavailable environments explicitly; do not present fixture results as real consumption. | Maintainer PR review where toolchains are installed; not a role-sandbox blocker beyond the approved-input mismatch. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

After corrected approval, use these commands from the repository root. Proposed tests below must exist before recording a passing run. Use prepared toolchain/dependency mounts and scratch Go build cache; do not request network access.

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox -run '^Test(SandboxedRestoreAdapters|SandboxedRestorePublication|SandboxedRestoreSelection|DependencyCache.*|DependencyTableSafety|EveryMountedEcosystemIsClassified|NoPrefetchEcosystemsKeepHostMounts|SharedHostCachesMountsHostGoModCache|GoPrefetchReadsBaseNotWorktree|RestoreLinuxFlags|RestoreLinuxBoundary|RestoreLinuxFailureCleanup)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/node ./internal/harness -run '^Test(RestoreRegistrySettings|DependencyCacheModeFromProfile|PrivateGoModulesResolvesRegisteredRepository|ConfigCannotEnableSharedHostCaches)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^Test(PreflightStopsBeforeClaimWhenDependencyCacheFails|AgentsStartWithPrefetchedDependencies|PrepareAgentDependenciesOnlyForNativeIsolation|AgentDependenciesUseRepositoryPolicy|SandboxedRestore.*)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/validation -run '^Test(ValidateUsesValidatorDependencyCache|ValidatePrefetchFailureStopsBeforeChecks|CleanCheckEnvUsesDependencyCaches|ValidatorDependenciesUseRepositoryPolicy|CleanCheckEnvHasNoPrefetchCredentials|SandboxedRestore.*)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(DoctorReportsDependencyCacheModes|NodeStatusReportsDependencyCacheMode|DoctorReportsPrivateGoModules|SandboxedRestore.*)$' -count=1
go vet ./internal/sandbox ./internal/node ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation ./internal/cli ./internal/contract ./internal/harness
```

Run gofmt on changed Go files and verify `gofmt -l <changed-Go-files>` returns empty output. Review documentation links and parse changed shell snippets with `bash -n`; verify examples against registered CLI flags and final NodeProfile fields. No new CLI flags are needed.

Expected focused test duration: 1–5 minutes each command; vet up to five minutes with prepared caches. Record exit status, duration, individual skipped runtime tests and reasons. Pure policy/selection/publication fixtures must run even if a Linux boundary integration test cannot run. A skipped boundary fixture is missing evidence, never a passing boundary observation; retain it for capable CI or PR review without expanding permissions.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently map the final source to every row above, including .NET prerequisite resolution, actual harness selection for both agent and validator, approved-base materialization, policy authority, generation identity, root-bound publication, mount replacement and the launch/fallback distinction. Check adversarial tests exercise the production path and would detect the old integration behavior. Review preservation of other adapters, native/OCI behavior and the unchanged transport boundary. Review docs/changelog for setup accuracy.

Reuse passing developer commands when their recorded source identity still matches. Run only targeted missing/failing cases or checks affected by later source changes; do not rerun whole packages merely to establish independent ownership. Record independent findings and reused evidence in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`.

## Coordinator-owned policy and long-running checks

The compiled approved validation policy is a coordinator reference, not an agent checklist. Coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once after role work on the final candidate. This includes format/build/vet/staticcheck and applicable security/regression checks; do not add a second full or race suite.

| Check expected to exceed five minutes | Single owner | Expected duration | Reuse and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete trusted-base required policy, including CLI regression shards | coordinator | 15–60 minutes total; individual check limits remain those in trusted policy | Later publication/review reuses coordinator validation artifacts tied to claim, policy and final candidate identity. Developer/tester do not rerun it. |

Record focused developer evidence in `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md`, tester evidence in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`: exact command, status, duration, source commit/tree or changed-file content digests, approved base, relevant fixture configuration and skip reasons. Reuse requires matching relevant source/test/config digests; later changes, failures or unresolved coverage concerns justify only the affected repeat commands. Agent evidence is advisory and never satisfies claim-bound validation or publication.
